info.title: Spendifico API
info.description:
The HTTP contract of the Spendifico backend.

Generated from the NestJS code at build time, committed as `backend/openapi.json`, and
the only source of the frontend response types in `frontend/src/types/api.d.ts`.
Do not edit either by hand: run `npm run api:sync` from the repo root.

Every operation can additionally answer **500** with `ErrorResponseDto`, via the global
exception filter. It is stated once here rather than per operation: it is the same
non-actionable fact everywhere, and repeating it would widen every generated response type.

bearer.description: The raw session token returned by POST /api/auth/verify. Opaque: 256 random bits, base64url, looked up by hash server-side.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, e.g. `EUR`. Case-insensitive on the way in, stored and returned uppercase.

monthlyBudget.description:
Major units (e.g. 2000.50). Stored as integer cents. The cap is not a
product judgment: it keeps the cents conversion far inside JS safe-integer
range while staying generous for zero-decimal currencies, whose budgets
carry many digits.

monthStartDay.description: Capped at 28 so the day exists in every month.

categories.description:
The starter chips picked on screen 03, by name.

Required but allowed to be empty: A4 records that no minimum is enforced,
and a user who deselects everything is making a valid choice. Required
rather than optional so a frontend that stops sending the field fails
loudly instead of silently seeding nothing.

message.description: String for most errors; an array for class-validator's field messages.

token.description:
The raw token, exactly as it arrived in the link. 43 characters in practice
(256 bits, base64url); the bound is loose enough not to encode that here
while still keeping a megabyte body from ever reaching a hash function.

The raw session token, to be sent back as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

The only place it ever appears in a response - the server keeps its hash.
The frontend puts it in an httpOnly, first-party cookie and forwards it
server-side; it must never reach client-side JavaScript.

expiresAt.description: ISO 8601. Fixed at issue: using the session does not extend it.
ISO 8601, the same instant verification returned.

monthStartDay.description:
Day of the month the budgeting period starts on, 1-28. Every period-scoped
read derives its month window from this at query time, so changing it
re-buckets history rather than rewriting anything.

email.description: The login identifier. Lives in the central directory, not the profile row.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, uppercase. Display only - amounts are stored in minor units.

monthlyBudget.description: Major units (e.g. 2000.5). Stored as integer cents; converted on the way out.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, e.g. `EUR`. Case-insensitive on the way in, stored and returned uppercase.

monthlyBudget.description: Major units (e.g. 2000.50), as at registration. Stored as integer cents.

monthStartDay.description: Capped at 28 so the day exists in every month.

email.description:
The login identifier. Changing it changes where future login links are sent
(AC6); links already in flight to the old address keep working.

amount.description:
Major units (e.g. 12.50), stored as integer cents. Positive: this app
records spending, and direction is not a per-row choice.

date.description:
The calendar day the money was spent, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Stored verbatim.

Backdating is ordinary and supported: the month a transaction belongs to is
derived from this at read time, so a date in a past month lands in that
month rather than the one it was entered in.

categoryId.description: An existing category of this user's. An unknown id is a 404, not a 400.

amount.description: Major units (e.g. 12.5). Stored as integer cents; converted on the way out.

date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, exactly the string that was stored.

note.description: Null when the transaction has no note, never absent.

updatedAt.description:
ISO 8601. Within a millisecond of `createdAt` until the first edit, not
necessarily equal to it: the two columns default from independent `new Date()`
calls, so an insert can straddle a millisecond boundary. Do not use equality
of the two to mean "never edited".

date.description: `YYYY-MM-DD`, as on create. Inline regex for the `pattern` lift.

note.description:
The one nullable field, and so the one that keeps `@IsOptional()`: null is
a meaningful value here rather than a mistake, and it means "clear the
note".

isFallback.description: True for the one `Uncategorized` category every account has. It cannot be deleted or renamed, deleting any other category moves its transactions here, and the transaction form preselects it.

monthlyCap.description: Major units. Null means uncapped, which is not a cap of 0.

spent.description: Major units spent in this category during the current period.

percentUsed.description: Percentage of the cap used, unrounded. Null when uncapped. Round it for display; the status is decided on cents, so rounding cannot disagree with it.

remaining.description: Major units still available. Null when uncapped or already over; `over` carries the excess instead.

over.description: Major units spent beyond the cap. Null unless the status is `over`.

status.description: Decided on cents, not on `percentUsed`. `uncapped` when there is no cap.

allocated.description: Major units. The sum of every live category cap; uncapped categories contribute nothing, so this can sit well below the budget for someone who caps little.

unallocated.description: Major units, `monthlyBudget - allocated`. **Can be negative**: nothing prevents caps from exceeding the budget (A43), and the figure is returned unclamped so the excess is recoverable.

color.description: Hex, `#RRGGBB`. The eight category colors come from Figma frame 03.

monthlyCap.description: Major units (e.g. 400.00), stored as integer cents. Omit for no cap.

icon.description: A name from the frontend's own icon set. Never resolved to an asset here.

note.description: Captured, but surfaces on no screen today (CED-4, A42).

monthlyCap.description: Major units. `null` clears the cap, leaving the category uncapped.
